'''Gilles I. Pisier''' (born 18 November 1950) is a professor of mathematics at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] and a distinguished professor and A.G. and M.E. Owen Chair of Mathematics at the [[Texas A&M University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.jussieu.fr/~pisier|title=Gilles Pisier|accessdate=14 April 2010|archive-date=10 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101210164148/http://www.math.jussieu.fr/~pisier/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tamu.edu/directory/formalpg.php?user=pisier|title=Gilles Pisier|publisher=Texas A&M University|accessdate=5 March 2010}}</ref> He is known for his contributions to several fields of mathematics, including [[functional analysis]], [[probability theory]], [[harmonic analysis]], and [[operator theory]]. He has also made fundamental contributions to the theory of  [[C*-algebras]].<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199807/comm-ostrowski.pdf|title=Nesterenko and Pisier Share Ostrowski Prize|date=August 1998|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=5 March 2010}}</ref> Gilles is the younger brother of French actress [[Marie-France Pisier]].

==Research==
Pisier has obtained many fundamental results in various parts of mathematical analysis.

===Geometry of Banach spaces===
{{See also|Banach space|Random vector}}
In the "local theory of [[Banach space]]s", Pisier and Bernard Maurey developed the theory of [[Rademacher type]], following its use in [[probability theory]] by J. Hoffman–Jorgensen and in the characterization of [[Hilbert space]]s among [[Banach space]]s by S.&nbsp;Kwapień. Using [[probability theory|probability]] in [[vector space]]s, Pisier proved that [[Reflexive space#Super-reflexive space|super-reflexive]] Banach spaces can be renormed with the [[modulus of convexity|modulus]] of [[Uniformly convex space|uniform convexity]] having "power type".<ref>{{cite book|author=Beauzamy, Bernard|title=Introduction to Banach Spaces and their Geometry|year=1985 |orig-date=1982|edition=Second revised|publisher=North-Holland|mr=889253|isbn=0-444-86416-4}}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Pisier |first=Gilles | title= Martingales with values in uniformly convex spaces | journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] | volume=20 | year=1975 | issue=3–4 | pages=326–350 | doi = 10.1007/BF02760337 | doi-access=free | mr=394135 |s2cid=120947324 }}</ref> His work (with [[Per Enflo]] and [[Joram Lindenstrauss]]) on the "three–space problem" influenced the work on [[Fréchet space|quasi–normed]] spaces by [[Nigel Kalton]].

===Operator theory===
{{See also|Operator theory|Operator space}}
Pisier transformed the area of [[operator space]]s. In the 1990s, he solved two long-standing open problems. In the theory of [[C*-algebra]]s, he solved, jointly with [[Marius Junge]], the problem of the uniqueness of C*&nbsp;-norms on the [[tensor product]] of two copies of&nbsp;''B(H)'', the bounded linear operators on a [[Hilbert space]]&nbsp;''H''. He and Junge were able to produce two such tensor norms that are nonequivalent.<ref name="ams" /> In&nbsp;1997, he constructed an [[Operator (mathematics)|operator]] that was polynomially bounded but not similar to a [[Contraction (operator theory)|contraction]], answering a famous question of [[Paul Halmos]].

==Awards==
He was an invited speaker at the 1983 [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]]<ref>{{cite book|author=Pisier, Gilles|chapter=Finite Rank Projections on Banach Spaces and a Conjecture of Grothendieck|year=1983|title=Proceedings of the ICM, 1983|pages=1027–1039|chapter-url=https://www.imj-prg.fr/wp-content/uploads/2020/prix/pisier1983.pdf}}</ref> and 
a plenary speaker at the 1998 [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|website=mathunion.org|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Pisier}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Pisier, Gilles|chapter=Operator spaces and similarity problems|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. I|year=1998|pages=429–452|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011731000}}</ref> In 1997, Pisier received the [[Ostrowski Prize]] for this work. He is also a recipient of the Grands Prix de l'Académie des Sciences de Paris in 1992 and the [[Salem Prize]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/dls/2001/pisier.html|title=UCLA Distinguished Lecturers|publisher=[[University of California]]|accessdate=13 March 2010|archive-date=28 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101228191528/http://www.math.ucla.edu/dls/2001/pisier.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-05-05.</ref>

==Books==
Pisier has authored several books and monographs in the fields of [[functional analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]], and [[operator theory]]. Among them are:
* {{cite book | last=Pisier | first=Gilles | title=The volume of convex bodies and Banach space geometry | publisher=Cambridge University Press | publication-place=Cambridge | date=1989 | isbn=0-521-36465-5 | oclc=19130153}}<ref>{{cite journal|author=Burkholder, Donald L.|authorlink=Donald Burkholder|title=Review: ''The Volume of Convex Bodies and Banach Space Geometry'', by G. Pisier|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|year=1991|volume=25|issue=1|pages=140–145|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1991-16046-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* {{cite book | last=Pisier | first=Gilles | title=Introduction to Operator Space Theory | publisher=Cambridge University Press | date=25 August 2003 | isbn=978-0-521-81165-1 | doi=10.1017/cbo9781107360235}}
* {{cite book | last=Pisier | first=Gilles | title=The operator Hilbert space OH, complex interpolation and tensor norms | publication-place=Providence, Rhode Island | date=1996 | isbn=978-1-4704-0170-2 | oclc=891396783}}
* {{cite book | last=Pisier | first=Gilles | author2=Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences | title=Factorization of linear operators and geometry of Banach spaces | publisher=Published for the Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences by the American Mathematical Society | publication-place=Providence, R.I. | date=1986 | isbn=0-8218-0710-2 | oclc=12419949}}
* {{cite book | last=Pisier | first=Gilles | title=Lecture Notes in Mathematics | chapter=Similarity Problems and Completely Bounded Maps | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | publication-place=Berlin, Heidelberg | year=1996 | volume=1618 | isbn=978-3-540-60322-1 | issn=0075-8434 | doi=10.1007/978-3-662-21537-1}}
* {{cite book | last1=Marcus | first1=Michael B. | last2=Pisier | first2=Gilles | title=Random Fourier Series with Applications to Harmonic Analysis. (AM-101) | publisher=Princeton University Press | date=31 December 1982 | isbn=978-1-4008-8153-6 | doi=10.1515/9781400881536}}<ref>{{cite journal|author=Rider, Daniel|authorlink=Daniel Rider|title=Review: ''Random Fourier Series with Applications to Harmonic Analysis'', by M. B. Marcus and G. Pisier|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|year=1983|volume=8|issue=2|pages=353–356|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1983-15119-4|doi-access=free}}</ref>
